items.title: Live: Iran says Trump's plan to support ships through strait would violate ceasefire
items.description: A senior Iranian official says any US attempt to interfere in the Strait of Hormuz would violate the ceasefire after Donald Trump says the US will try to free up ships there. Follow live.

items.title: Kumanjayi Little Baby remembered across NT after 'unthinkable trauma'
items.description: The Northern Territory is continuing to grieve the short life of a five-year-old girl today, with crowds in Alice Springs to pay tribute by donning pink — her favourite colour.

items.title: 'Ugly displays of hostility' towards Jews focus of royal commisson hearings
items.description: The Jewish community's experiences of antisemitism will be put on display on the first day of the royal commission triggered by the Bondi Beach terror attack last year.

items.title: A hacker built a tool to track police officers. Then he tried to warn them
items.description: A security flaw means the location of devices used by police, potentially including undercover officers and those travelling home, is visible to anyone with a phone or laptop.

items.title: Tax windfall from Iran war to be pocketed in federal budget
items.description: The extra tax revenue generated by the Iran war will be saved in its entirety, as the government downplays major cost-of-living relief in next week's federal budget — though the treasurer warns those gains will be small.

items.title: Trump's former personal lawyer Rudy Giuliani in critical condition
items.description: Former New York mayor and US President Donald Trump's former personal lawyer Rudy Giuliani is in hospital in a critical condition.

items.title: Three die after suspected hantavirus outbreak on cruise ship
items.description: A suspected outbreak of hantavirus, which is spread by contact with rat and mice faeces, has killed three people on a cruise ship.

items.title: A new poll tells us a lot about One Nation's new-found support
items.description: A new poll asks Australians specifically about One Nation and the results show that rather than being a flash in the pan, the minor party's freight train may be a more lasting phenomenon.

items.title: Australian businesses falling victim to new type of fraud
items.description: Higher inflation, a war in the Middle East, and a ban on surcharges are crippling small businesses. Now they are falling victim to a modern crime.

items.title: Live: Japan's Takaichi welcomed to parliament ahead of Albanese meeting
items.description: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae has been welcomed to federal parliament ahead of a meeting with Anthony Albanese. Follow live.

items.title: Australia's most remote communities losing essential services due to price of fuel
items.description: Cultural obligations and essential services are being impacted by the cost of fuel in Australia's most remote communities.

items.title: Busloads of tourists turn quiet street into 'internet sensation'
items.description: For years, the residents of Tasman Drive in Gerringong knew they lived in a stunningly beautiful part of the world, but then social media discovered it too.

items.title: We're headed into an AI fog as the automation arms race begins
items.description: Artificial intelligence might be driving growth for data centre companies, but society is unprepared for the long-term risks posed to the rest of us.

items.title: Live: NAB profit drops as bank warns of Middle East uncertainty
items.description: The ASX has slipped on opening, despite strong corporate earnings propelling the S&P 500 to a new record close. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Is classical music's decline a myth? What the numbers say
items.description: As Australians vote for the greatest classical music of all time, we look at who is listening, how classical music is evolving, and how it fills the world around us.

items.title: What can you use your personal leave for?
items.description: People employed on a permanent basis in Australia are entitled to 10 days' paid personal leave a year to help navigate illness, caring responsibilities, or family emergencies. But what are the different types of personal leave and when can you use them?

items.title: Quiz: Can you name the typo on the $50 note?
items.description: Take a trip back in time with this week's history quiz.

items.title: SA treasurer attacks Chinese government over smelter woes
items.description: The SA treasurer claims a foreign government is undermining the profitability of the struggling Port Pirie metal smelter.

items.title: No-grounds evictions banned in WA housing policy shift
items.description: Under the proposed laws, landlords will no longer be allowed to terminate a tenant's lease without giving a reason.

items.title: Victorian teachers call off this week's strike as pay talks progress
items.description: The Australian Education Union has suspended part of its industrial campaign, saying negotiations over a new pay offer have been more productive.

items.title: Russian woman's husband beat her but police were no help, so she wrote to Putin
items.description: Domestic violence and abuse have been described as an "epidemic" in multiple countries, but analysts argue there is something that sets Russia apart: the government is making things worse.

items.title: Worker shortage sees people struggle in 'most extreme form of homelessness'
items.description: Victoria needs almost five times as many outreach field workers to support people who are sleeping rough, according to a study by the Council to Homeless Persons.

items.title: Small business faces $500,000 bill to go electric amid gas switch-off
items.description: ATCO Australia tells 8,000 customers they will need to find new energy sources or switch to bottled gas as it prepares to decommission its Great Southern gas network in WA.

items.title: Parents of 14yo athlete who died suddenly work to prevent future heartbreaks
items.description: Two Canberra parents rocked by the sudden death of their teenage son are trying to help him leave a life-saving legacy.

items.title: Housing provider blamed tenant for soaked carpet, then regulator stepped in
items.description: Despite unsafe and unusable bathrooms, cockroach infestations eating through wiring and constantly damp carpets, some Tasmanian public housing tenants are having to get the regulator to intervene in order to get solutions.
